YES AND YES, a million times YES to a C.C. puzzle, in all the world's languages! But I'm a little sad that it was over too soon. I went slowly, enjoying it, but it still took me only 10 minutes and made me wish it went on. I almost felt nostalgic for when I first started solving a few years back and even a Monday would take me forever. Something like "Sound asleep?" would have found me in deep thought, having to get SNORE from the crosses, and then studying the connection between clue and entry before I'd learned about question marks, misdirects, and all that good stuff that makes NYT crosswords so special. And C.C.'s puzzles are always a treat, beautifully constructed, and made to be savored. Thank you so much for each and every one of them! (A song by the band YES would be the most appropriate for this puzzle, but Jon Anderson's voice is not a favorite of mine. And so I leave you with Pink Floyd instead) – https://youtu.be/KmIkJgHISMo?is=MJXGSyFeYyAwst8P

3 minutes! Personal best!

Of course it takes me an average of 40 minutes to solve the Sunday puzzle.  So don’t think it’s that impressive.
Smooth as silk.   Brava!

A nice Monday meander.

Incidentally, my wife and I often call ourselves Meanderthals cause that's what we like doing when travelling overseas or exploring previously unvisited parts of our own beautiful city.
New Monday record! 3 min 20 sec :)
Today I finished the crossword before I even looked at the Wordplay article AND I didn’t Google anything. Feeling highly accomplished 🤩

This was the closest I have ever gotten to solving a Monday with just acrosses (maybe it helps that two of the themes were down.) TROLLS did me in—I couldn’t get GNOMES out of my head, and S-S, -AND and -ETS had too many possibilities. The fact is, KOA almost did me in for the whole puzzle—I had KIA and had to flyspeck. KOA and ROAN was a Natick for me, and I confess I thought Chappell was a last name. That’s all on me.

Anyways, terrific Monday, it was SUPERCUTe which is handy because Supercuts is my favorite HAIrcut cHAIn (and the Japanese doubly agree).

Always a pleasure to solve a puzzle by CC. I did trip myself up a bit by spelling LOUIE as LOUIs and deciding that the theme answer was YES, YES, YES* without verifying. And here are a few too many Yeahs. https://youtu.be/nGbWU8S3vzs?si=RV6TthcxFAK4te2k *OT Shout-out to Meg Ryan.

(I wish there was a Ulysses reference in this puzzle.) 

When I watched news on TV or read the local paper, neither of which I've done in years, I'd see mention of the annual Dapper Dan Dinner, always at some old-timey downtown club, with photos and footage of big beefy grinning middle aged men in padded dacron suits patting each other on the back, as they lifted their mugs to salute the Dapper Dan Man of the Year, voted as the biggest, beefiest, most ill-fitting suit-owning, with a heart that pumped pure gold, dapperest most polyesterized dude Pittsburgh would ever see the likes of til the following year. There's nothing I miss more than reportage of that banquet. (I always thought he must have been a Pittsburgh dandy in times of yore, but now I know that Dapper Dan is a mythological creature known across the globe, so this puzzle has been quite enlightening). Also, plus one for [Sound asleep?]!

"Harmonizer at Disney" could have been a clue for 16A, since the roaming barbershop quartets at Florida and California are called the Dapper Dans. There is also an unofficial Dapper Day weekend for those who care to dress up in vintage outfits coming up on December 5th at Magic Kingdom and 6th at Hollywood Studios in Florida.

Always nice to have a CC puzzle, and this was one of my faster solves. Thanks!
Nice!

Not a fan of OSLO being clued as "Capital with fjord tours."   My understanding is that there are no true fjords in Oslo; the fjords we all think of are several hours away.  The word "fjord" in Norwegian can refer to a bunch of different waterways, but those aren't actual fjords.

To me, this is an example of a clue that's trying too hard to be different, and by doing so, sacrifices clarity.  Now if "Capital with fjord tours" had led to KRONE, I would have thought it was a great clue.

Don’t let Mondays get you down!

Remain horizontal!

Take the “Across clues only” challenge!

I didn’t look at any Down clues and managed to finish today’s puzzle (in 9:37). 

Restricting yourself to one half of the clues makes it trickier and tense and a shade more challenging. Highly recommended if you find Mondays (and maybe even Tuesdays) too straightforward, and you’d like to tease out the tease a bit. 

It’s all just for fun, so ignore me if this is not your idea of fun. Otherwise, let me lay down the challenge! (Or lie across it??)

Otherwise a Monday.
Fun 👍

You can get a third page easily enough via the standalone Games App, but there is no easy way of finding this page if you’re on the NYT app — on an iPhone anyway (my personal preference).

Now, can someone explain KISSCAM for me? I know what it is, having seen it in many films etc, plus I guess it was the conveyance for the infamous Coldplay cheaters outing. But what I don’t get is, why? Why do you have it? What’s the connection with sport? Is it a specific sport or just arena sport in general? 
I cannot imagine such a thing working in the UK. You aim a camera at the average football crowd and a kiss is most definitely not the reaction you’d get!

I like to point out from time to time, because I’m so impressed, that English is not CC’s native language, and here she is, creator of 85 NYT puzzles and many more elsewhere.

(HAI)L (HAI)L, CC!

Today she sprinkled the grid with loveliness -- JAMJARS, SCREEDS, NOSHED, MIMOSA, MEANDER – and bolstered the global theme with international flavor (PAOLO, EIN, KPH, ISIS, UAE, OSLO, OSSO, HABANERO, MAPO, ESO, MARINARA, ASTI).

I liked the very short tale: I SEE / UNDO / REDO.  Also lovely was the abutting schwa-enders cascading down the grid – MARINARA / MIMOSA / THETA.  Then there was the sweet serendipity of the SI-SI theme answer being crossed by a backward SISI.

Terrific idea for a theme, CC, and a terrific execution.  Thank you once again, for a splendid outing!

My late and brilliant horticulturist friend would be at pains to remind us: Although often confused in US supermarkets, yams and sweet potatoes are entirely different, unrelated plants with distinct physical traits, tastes, and botanical families. Virtually all orange-fleshed roots sold as "yams" in American grocery stores are actually sweet potatoes. Learn more at: https://www.google.com/search?client=safari&rls=en&q=yam+vs.+sweet+potato&ie=UTF-8&oe=UTF-8
